thread:
incident-bot: PAGER -> SSE+fncall: elevated disconnects + tool-call parse errors detected. alert: 12 customers impacted, 2312345678 UTC start, auto-escalation to on-call. Severity: P2.

alice_oncall: ack'd. I'm on it, switching to incident channel. collecting initial scope: which regions and models?

bob_sre: seeing spikes in downstream 502s from the runtime in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Errors correlate with large multipart tool-call payloads. attaching grep sample.

carla_runtime: FYI, we've been rolling the new SSE client parser in eu-west last night (flag: streaming-parser-v2). possible link.

alice_oncall: steps: 1) gather logs + timeline 2) triage hotfix/rollback 3) customer comms. I'll own coordination.

bob_sre: log snippet (recent 30s from runtime):
```
[2026-03-15T18:01:03Z] conn_id=abc123 SSE_DISCONNECT reason=client_reset code=1006 route=/v1/stream
[2026-03-15T18:01:03Z] conn_id=abc123 toolcall_parse_error: unexpected EOF while parsing tool payload
[2026-03-15T18:01:04Z] upstream=kv_cache shard=3 err=kv_timeout
[2026-03-15T18:01:05Z] conn_id=def456 SSE_DISCONNECT reason=idle_timeout code=1001
```

carla_runtime: adding more context — parser v2 is stricter about trailing commas and chunked JSON boundaries. It will reject partial frames rather than waiting. Could explain parse_error spike.

dave_platform: can we confirm if the client SDK shipped yesterday included streaming-parser-v2 by default? I remember a canary.

carla_runtime: yes, we flipped streaming-parser-v2 on for 10% canary in eu-west-1 at 17:40 UTC and rolled to 50% at 17:58 for that region per deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: release/streaming-parser-v2 @ 2026-03-15T17:40:12Z -> eu-west-1 (10%), 2026-03-15T17:58:27Z -> eu-west-1 (50%). No rollouts to us-west-2 yet.

alice_oncall: hypothesis A: parser v2 stricter semantics causing clients with chunked/partial frames to be disconnected -> downstream toolcall parse errors and higher 502s.

alice_oncall: hypothesis B: unrelated KV shard pressure causing timeouts resulting in partial writes and client disconnects; parser sees truncated payloads.

bob_sre: evidence for A: temporal correlation between canary increase and errors in eu-west-1 logs. evidence for B: there's a small KV latency bump around same time but not as large as previous incidents. attaching kv graphs link: https://grafana.redwood/kv/graph?from=2312345620&to=2312345720

erin_support: customer impact quick summary for ops: 12 customers had 5xxs or incomplete streamed responses. Top 3 impacted are: AcmeInc (chat), BlueFin (agent), Edu.ai (grading). No payment or data loss reported. Some customers opened support tickets and one tweeted an error screenshot.

janet_cs: drafting customer note — short, non-technical: "We experienced streaming interruptions affecting some requests between 17:40–18:05 UTC. Our engineers are investigating; if you saw truncated responses, please retry and contact support. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

carla_runtime: pairing logs — full parser traces (sensitive) uploaded to secure bucket: s3://internal-logs/incidents/2312345678/parser-traces.gz (access granted to on-call + SRE). grep sample for bad frames:
```
frame: {"tool": "search", "args": [ ... partial data
// missing closing bracket
```

alice_oncall: live mitigation options: 1) rollback streaming-parser-v2 to previous parser in eu-west-1 2) apply lenient-mode gate (feature flag) 3) increase client backoff + drop canary. Which is lowest blast radius?

dave_platform: rollback is fastest and reversible. initiating rollback plan if SRE+runtime agree. I can trigger a 10->0 rollback via deploy-bot in 2 minutes.

bob_sre: while rollback in progress, enable request-level fallback: if parse_error -> treat as transient and reconnect without failing caller (server-driven reconnect). I'll draft a runtime patch but need ~20min.

carla_runtime: rollback will restore previous parser behavior that tolerated partial frames. downside: we lose stricter validation, but reduces customer impact. I support rollback.

alice_oncall: decision: rollback streaming-parser-v2 in eu-west-1 now. dave, please execute. bob/carla will watch logs for improvement. janet/erin will update customers.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: release/streaming-parser-v2 -> eu-west-1 scale 50%->0% at 2026-03-15T18:02:10Z by dave_platform.

bob_sre: monitoring logs... initial signs show drop in parse_error events within 30s. continuing to track.

carla_runtime: kv latency unchanged; this makes hypothesis A more likely (parser change) than B.

alice_oncall: timeline so far (building):
- 17:40 UTC: parser-v2 canary 10% (eu-west-1)
- 17:58 UTC: canary 50% (eu-west-1)
- 18:00 UTC: incident-bot alerted elevated 5xx + parse errors
- 18:02 UTC: rollback started
- 18:03 UTC: initial parse_errors dropping in eu-west-1

erin_support: customer note sent to impacted customers and added priority ticket for AcmeInc.

janet_cs: posted public brief to status page draft: "Partial streaming interruptions affecting some customers in eu-west-1. Engineers reverted a recent parser change; monitoring.
Next update in 30m."

bob_sre: next steps for RCA thread: - collect sample of malformed frames from clients - confirm if SDK versions sending chunked frames are within canary cohort - reproduce locally with parser-v2 + chunked payloads

carla_runtime: I'll pull build artifacts and run parser-v2 against the malformed frames. also will add enhanced logging around frame boundaries to catch partial writes.

- bob_sre: validate metrics and confirm dropoff, prepare graphs for RCA (ETA 45m)
